Consult Summary:
- Telephone consult for acute-onset left arm paralysis with left facial tingling, dysarthria, and dysphagia; high concern for acute stroke; emergency ambulance activated for transfer to hospital.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden inability to move the left arm (painless) upon waking this morning (~1 hour before call), with left facial tingling, difficulty swallowing, and speech changes (slower, harder to produce).
- Timeline:
  - On waking today: Noted complete inability to move left arm; left facial tingling started at the same time.
  - During call: Symptoms persisted; patient reports speech is getting a bit harder.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Left facial tingling; dysphagia (difficulty swallowing); speech changes (slowed, effortful).
  - Negative: No left leg symptoms; no hand discoloration; no coldness of the hand; no pain; patient has not noticed facial asymmetry.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None reported.
- Prior episodes: None reported.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.

Medications:
- Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Losartan — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Amlodipine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergy: Penicillin.

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Tobacco: Former smoker.
- Alcohol: Drinks beer; a few drinks on weekends and a couple more during the week (pints); exact quantities not documented.
- No other substance use mentioned.

Family History:
- Father with heart disease; further details not known.

Physical Examination:
- Not performed (telephone consultation). No vitals recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during the call.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute focal neurological deficit concerning for acute cerebrovascular event (suspected stroke)
  - Assessment: Sudden painless left arm paralysis with left facial paresthesia, dysphagia, and dysarthria, onset ~1 hour prior to call on waking. High suspicion for acute stroke.
  - Plan:
    - Emergency services activated; ambulance arranged to patient’s home for urgent transfer to emergency department/stroke evaluation.
    - Patient advised to unlock front door and sit in the hallway for access.
    - Clinician remained on the line until ambulance arrival.
    - Anticipated ED actions discussed with patient: stroke team assessment and consideration of acute therapy as indicated.

- General Plan items:
  - No further at-home interventions advised prior to ambulance arrival.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; focused neurological examination; last-known-well time beyond “on waking” clarification; medication doses/routes/frequencies; anticoagulant/antiplatelet use status; past surgical history; stroke risk assessment details (e.g., lipid status); swallow screen/NPO guidance not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear; telephone-only limits examination and objective findings.
